# Introduction

[MetaboLights](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metabolights/) deposits every study as a
set of ISA-TAB files: an *investigation* file with the study-level metadata,
a *sample* file, one *assay* file per analytical assay linking samples to
data files, and one *metabolite assignment file* (MAF) per assay with the
reported metabolites and their abundances per sample. The
`r Biocpkg("MsBackendMetaboLights")` package [@Rainer2024] gives access to
these files and to the raw MS data.

`r Biocpkg("mtbls2mztabm")` turns the ISA-TAB files of a study into an
[mzTab-M 2.1](https://github.com/HUPO-PSI/mzTab-M) file [@Hoffmann2019], the
exchange format of the community for quantitative metabolomics results. It
does so in two steps that each leave a file behind, which can be inspected,
edited and reused:

```
                   ┌─ factors, samples, runs, metadata ─▶ <study>.toml    ─▶ MTD ─┐
MetaboLights ID ───┤                                                              ├─▶ mzTab-M
                   └─ metabolite assignment file (MAF) ─▶ <study>.parquet ─▶ SML ─┘
```

1. The study factors (the *sample groups*), the samples, the MS runs and the
   study metadata of one assay are saved to a [TOML](https://toml.io) file
   (`mtbls_factors_to_toml()`), the MAF of the assay to an
   [Apache Parquet](https://parquet.apache.org) file
   (`mtbls_maf_to_parquet()`).
2. The *metadata* section (`MTD`) of the mzTab-M file is built from the TOML
   file (`mtbls_toml_to_mtd()`) and the *small molecule* section (`SML`) from
   the Parquet file (`mtbls_parquet_to_sml()`), both with the *RmzTabM*
   package. `mtd_sml_to_mztabm()` combines them and `RmzTabM::writeMzTabM()`
   writes the file.

`mtbls_to_mztabm()` runs all of this from a study identifier.

The study used throughout is
[MTBLS103](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metabolights/MTBLS103), an NMR and LC-MS
metabolomics study of serum from adolescents with hyperinsulinaemic androgen
excess [@Samino2015]. Its ISA-TAB files are shipped with the package and are
read from there with the argument `path`, so that everything below runs
without network access. Without `path`, every function reads the files of
the study from the MetaboLights FTP server. A second study of a different
kind, the GC-MS study MTBLS40, is exported in the same way towards the end.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("mtbls2mztabm")
```

```{r load}
library(mtbls2mztabm)
ext <- system.file("extdata", "MTBLS103", package = "mtbls2mztabm")
assay <- "a_MTBLS103_ibanez_02_HILIC_mass_spectrometry.txt"
```

The `MTD` sections below are shown with a small helper that lists the fields
matching a pattern.

```{r helper}
show_mtd <- function(mtd, pattern, n = 64) {
    x <- mtd[grepl(pattern, mtd[, 1L]), , drop = FALSE]
    v <- ifelse(nchar(x[, 2L]) > n, paste0(substr(x[, 2L], 1L, n - 3L), "..."),
                x[, 2L])
    print(data.frame(field = x[, 1L], value = v), right = FALSE,
          row.names = FALSE)
}
```

# The study and its factors

The investigation file is returned as a named list of records.

```{r investigation}
inv <- mtbls_investigation("MTBLS103", path = ext)
inv[["Study Title"]]
inv[["Study Assay File Name"]]
```

MTBLS103 has one experimental factor, *HIAE*, with the levels `CTR`
(healthy controls), `HIAE` (patients at diagnosis) and `TREAT` (the same
patients after 18 months of treatment). These are the sample groups that
become the *study variables* of the mzTab-M file.

```{r factors}
mtbls_factors("MTBLS103", path = ext)
fv <- mtbls_factor_values("MTBLS103", path = ext)
table(fv$hiae)
```

# Step 1: the study description as TOML

`mtbls_factors_to_toml()` saves what the metadata section of the mzTab-M
file needs to the TOML file of one assay. Of the four assays of MTBLS103 the
HILIC LC-MS assay is used here; without `assayName` the first mass
spectrometry assay is chosen and named in a message.

```{r toml}
toml <- mtbls_factors_to_toml(
    "MTBLS103", file = file.path(tempdir(), "MTBLS103.toml"),
    assayName = assay, path = ext)
```

The file starts with the study metadata, the assay and MAF it belongs to,
and the instrument taken from the assay table.

```{r toml-study, echo = FALSE}
lns <- readLines(toml)
short <- function(x, n = 88)
    ifelse(nchar(x) > n, paste0(substr(x, 1, n - 3), "..."), x)
at <- function(pattern, n, i = 1L) lns[grep(pattern, lns)[i] + seq_len(n) - 1L]
cat(short(lns[seq_len(grep("^\\[\\[publication\\]\\]", lns)[1L] - 1L)]),
    sep = "\n")
```

The study factors follow with their definition from the investigation file
and the groups found in the assay. Every sample then lists the group it
belongs to in each factor, along with the organism and organism part, whose
ontology terms become the species and tissue of the sample in mzTab-M.

```{r toml-factor, echo = FALSE}
cat(short(c(at("^\\[\\[factor\\]\\]", 6L), "...",
            at("^\\[\\[sample\\]\\]", 11L), "...")), sep = "\n")
```

Finally, each row of the assay table is one *run*, which becomes an MS run
and an assay of the mzTab-M file. A run names its sample, its data file, its
scan polarity and the column of the MAF with its abundances.

```{r toml-run, echo = FALSE}
cat(short(c(at("^\\[\\[run\\]\\]", 7L), "...")), sep = "\n")
```

Because the file is plain text, a missing scan polarity or a wrong ontology
term of a study can be corrected before the next step. Here the title is
changed:

```{r toml-edit}
lns <- readLines(toml)
lns <- sub("^title = .*", "title = \"HDL maturation in adolescents with HIAE\"",
           lns)
edited <- file.path(tempdir(), "MTBLS103-edited.toml")
writeLines(lns, edited)
```

# Step 2: the metabolite assignment file as Parquet

`mtbls_maf_to_parquet()` saves the MAF of the assay, which lists the
reported metabolites and their abundance in every sample. The columns keep
their names and are given the same types for every study: the annotation
columns of the MAF are text and `mass_to_charge`, `retention_time` and the
abundances are numbers, also where a study leaves a column empty.

```{r parquet}
parquet <- mtbls_maf_to_parquet(
    "MTBLS103", file = file.path(tempdir(), "MTBLS103.parquet"),
    assayName = assay, path = ext)
maf <- nanoparquet::read_parquet(parquet)
dim(maf)
maf[, c("database_identifier", "chemical_formula",
        "metabolite_identification")]
```

The MAF of MTBLS103 reports 13 identified metabolites but no m/z or
retention time, so these columns are empty (`NA`).

# Step 3: the metadata section from the TOML file

`mtbls_toml_to_mtd()` reads the TOML file and builds the `MTD` section with
`RmzTabM::mtdFromSampleData()`. The result is a two-column matrix.

```{r mtd}
mtd <- mtbls_toml_to_mtd(toml)
dim(mtd)
show_mtd(mtd, "^(mzTab-ID|title|publication\\[1\\]|uri\\[1\\]|instrument)")
```

Every sample, MS run and assay of the study is listed, with the samples
referring to the species and tissue of the TOML file and the assays to their
samples and MS runs.

```{r mtd-sample}
show_mtd(mtd, "^(sample|ms_run|assay)\\[1\\]")
```

The groups of the study factor are the study variables. Each refers to the
assays of the samples of the group.

```{r mtd-sv}
show_mtd(mtd, "^study_variable(_group)?\\[[1-3]\\](-assay_refs)?$")
```

By default the first study factor that is not *Age* (which has one value per
participant) is used; the argument `factor` selects other or several
factors. The edited TOML file gives a different title:

```{r mtd-edited}
show_mtd(mtbls_toml_to_mtd(edited), "^title$")
```

# Step 4: the small molecule section from the Parquet file

`mtbls_parquet_to_sml()` builds the `SML` section with `RmzTabM::smlCreate()`:
one row per row of the MAF, with the abundances of the runs in the order of
the assays of the metadata section and, from the study variables of the
`MTD`, the average and variation of the abundances of each group. The TOML
file tells which MAF column belongs to which run. The `MTD` section is passed
on so that both sections agree.

```{r sml}
sml <- mtbls_parquet_to_sml(parquet, toml, mtd)
dim(sml)
head(sml[, c("SML_ID", "database_identifier", "chemical_name", "reliability",
             "abundance_assay[1]", "abundance_study_variable[1]")])
```

The annotation of the MAF (identifiers, formula, SMILES, InChI, name) is
taken over; placeholders such as `unknown` become `null`. What the MAF does
not provide is `null` as well, except for the `reliability` of the
identification, which mzTab-M requires for every small molecule. The MAF of
MTBLS103 gives none, so the lowest identification level of the Metabolomics
Standards Initiative, `4` (*unknown compound*), is reported, which claims
nothing about the confidence of the identification. The argument
`reliability` sets another level for molecules without one.

Two kinds of MAF content have no column in the `SML` section and are kept in
optional columns (`opt_global_*`): the retention time and m/z of a MAF that
reports them, and the annotations of molecules that have no identifier (the
mzTab-M validator requires the annotation lists to be as long as the
identifier list). The MAF of the GC-MS study MTBLS40 below has both.

# Step 5: the mzTab-M file

`mtd_sml_to_mztabm()` combines the two sections into an `MzTabM` object of the
*RmzTabM* package. It checks that they belong together and completes the
metadata with the compound databases found in the identifiers of the `SML`
(here ChEBI).

```{r merge}
m <- mtd_sml_to_mztabm(mtd, sml)
m
show_mtd(RmzTabM::mtd(m), "^(mzTab-profile|database)")
```

With `file`, the same function also writes the mzTab-M file with
`RmzTabM::writeMzTabM()`, which can equally be called on the returned object.
By default the written file is checked with the official mzTab-M validator,
which *RmzTabM* downloads when it is first used; `validate = FALSE` skips the
check.

```{r write}
f <- file.path(tempdir(), "MTBLS103-steps.mztab")
mtd_sml_to_mztabm(mtd, sml, file = f, validate = FALSE)
lns <- readLines(f)
c(MTD = sum(startsWith(lns, "MTD\t")), SML = sum(startsWith(lns, "SML\t")))
RmzTabM::readMzTabM(f, validate = FALSE)
```

# All steps at once

`mtbls_to_mztabm()` does all of the above in one call: it writes the TOML
and Parquet files next to the mzTab-M file (the arguments `toml` and
`parquet` put them elsewhere), builds both sections from them and writes the
mzTab-M file. With several assays and no `assayName` the first mass
spectrometry assay is chosen and named in the message.

```{r export}
out <- mtbls_to_mztabm(
    "MTBLS103", file = file.path(tempdir(), "MTBLS103.mztab"),
    assayName = assay, path = ext, validate = FALSE)
```

The file starts with the metadata section. Instrument, ion source and mass
analyzer come from the assay table, title, description and publication from
the investigation, and the compound database from the ChEBI identifiers of
the MAF.

```{r mztab-head}
lns <- readLines(out)
lns[grepl("^MTD\t(mzTab-ID|title|publication|instrument|database\\[1\\])",
          lns)]
```

The intermediate files and the `MzTabM` object are attached to the returned
path.

```{r attrs}
attr(out, "toml")
attr(out, "parquet")
attr(out, "mztabm")
```

Without `path` the files of the study are read from the MetaboLights FTP
server and, with the default `validate = TRUE`, the written file is checked
with the validator.

```{r remote, eval = FALSE}
mtbls_to_mztabm("MTBLS103", assayName = assay)
```

# A GC-MS study: MTBLS40

The same call serves any MetaboLights study with a mass spectrometry assay.
[MTBLS40](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metabolights/MTBLS40) is a GC-TOF-MS study
of *Arabidopsis thaliana* wild type and two mutants (`Col-0`, `mto1` and
`tt4`) [@Kusano2007]. Its assay table lists the raw netCDF data files only,
so these become the `ms_run`s of the mzTab-M file, the factor *Genotype*
becomes the study variables and the MAF contributes 171 small molecules with
retention times and, where identified, ChEBI identifiers.

```{r mtbls40}
ext40 <- system.file("extdata", "MTBLS40", package = "mtbls2mztabm")
out40 <- mtbls_to_mztabm(
    "MTBLS40", file = file.path(tempdir(), "MTBLS40.mztab"), path = ext40,
    validate = FALSE)
lns40 <- readLines(out40)
lns40[grepl("^MTD\t(ms_run\\[1\\]|instrument|study_variable\\[[1-4]\\]\t)",
            lns40)]
```

Many peaks of this MAF are not identified. Their label (here `PR-MST`) and the
retention time of all peaks are in optional columns of the `SML` section.

```{r mtbls40-sml}
sml40 <- RmzTabM::sml(attr(out40, "mztabm"))
head(sml40[, c("SML_ID", "database_identifier", "chemical_name",
               "opt_global_metabolite_identification",
               "opt_global_retention_time")])
```

# What the ISA-TAB files cannot provide

A MAF is a table of reported abundances, not a processing result. It has no
m/z and retention time of its features beyond the optional columns above, so
the file has an `SML` section but no *small molecule feature* section.
mzTab-M contacts require an ORCID, which ISA-TAB investigation files rarely
carry, so the contact section is left out unless one is present. Runs
without a data file get the location of the study as their `ms_run`
location, because mzTab-M needs one for every run. Runs without a value for
the study factor, such as quality control samples, form the study variable
`NA`, as *RmzTabM* defines it; giving them a value in the TOML file, for
example `QC`, changes this. The mean of a study variable is calculated from
the available abundances of its assays and is `null` only if all of them are
missing; its variation needs at least two available abundances.
